title: The Biggest Stick Figure Is Afraid of the Dark
altTitles: What's Down There? | Stick Figure Mini-Movie
Brick and the Thing in the Cave
description: Brick is the strongest of them all. He is also afraid of the dark. #stickfigure #animation #INKLIGHT
topic: L04 F7 heart mini-film + horror-lite chase: Brick alone in the cave, the shadow, Pebble the baby ink-mole

sections.label: S1 Hook: eyes in the dark
sections.videoPrompt: Cinematic 3D animated film. The characters are stylized stick figures: glossy matte-black ink bodies with uniform thin cylindrical limbs, perfectly round glossy black heads with no facial features except two small glowing oval eyes, and a thin emissive rim light in each character's signature color. They are set inside a hyper-detailed, physically lit 3D environment with volumetric light shafts, atmospheric haze, real materials, shallow depth of field and film-grade color grading. BRICK: a large black ink stick figure with thick heavy limbs (three times normal thickness) and a round glossy head, lime green (#7CFF4F) glowing eyes and rim light, a lime visor band across the eyes. Almost total darkness inside a cave; only Brick's lime green glowing eyes are visible, blinking open, glancing left and right, then widening in fear, while a very faint lime rim light traces his huge hunched shoulders. Static medium shot, 50mm, no light sources except the eye glow, damp rock barely visible. Avoid: text, letters, numbers, logos, mouths, noses, teeth, human faces, skin, hair, clothing beyond the listed accessories, extra limbs, fingers except three rounded nubs in close-ups, blood, gore, flat or empty backgrounds.

qc: L04: Drift — Brick's limb thickness and visor in near-black frames (the model may thin him); the lime rim stays lime under teal light (not cyan, which reads as Bolt). Limbs — S6 squeezing/sliding poses; S9 crawling (Pebble's paws vs Brick's arms merging). Faces — Pebble's snout must never grow a mouth or teeth (reject); the cracker 'nibble' is sparkle crumbs only. Style — darkness keeps readable rims (never pure black >1s except S1); the glowworm ceiling stays 3D volumetric, not a starfield wallpaper. Seams — S6 at 30s/60s: shadow direction and scale (and the creature is never shown, shadow only); S2 at 30s: the slab position holds; S7 at 30s: Brick's raised-fist pose held across the seam. Text — low; check rock walls for glyph-like cracks in S5. S7 reveal: ≥1.5s silence before the squeak; Pebble design fidelity is the payoff. Global gate (brief §0.3): accent hue shift >6 frames / missing accessory / size swap = re-roll; 3rd limb or fused limb ≥3 frames = re-roll; any mouth, nose, teeth, brows, skin or human face even 1 frame = reject; flat/white/empty bg, 2D look, lost rim light or blood = re-roll; stitch seam at 30s: position jump >5% width, lighting flip, prop changing hands, screen-direction reversal = regenerate the later segment; any legible or pseudo-glyph text in a plate = mask or re-roll (all real text is Remotion labels). Check sourceSpec width/height/duration every clip.
